title: Subretinal Implantation of RPE on a Carrier in Minipigs: Guidelines for Preoperative Preparations, Surgical Techniques, and Postoperative Care
protocol: Check for the surgical orientation of the eye and draw the fundus schemes.
Schematically divide the retina on the fundus drawing using a vertical line into temporal, nasal, and central regions.
Select only healthy animals without any behavioral or neurological pathology and with normal skin quality, body orifices, feces, and food consumption.
Have a skilled veterinarian perform the clinical observation and select the animals.
Inject intramuscularly 3 mg/kg BW of ceftiofur hydrochloride on the day of surgery.
Prepare tacrolimus-eluting polymer microspheres as described in Wang et al. and Sevc et al.
Ensure that the concentration of tacrolimus in the polymer microspheres is 51.3 mg/g as determined by HPLC.
Perform a subcutaneous injection of tacrolimus-loaded polymer microspheres at a dose of 0.25 mg/kg BW 6 days before eye surgery to impede cell graft rejection.
Inject animals intramuscularly on the day of surgery with 80 mg of depo-medrol and benzylpenicillin according to body weight.
Induce general anesthesia with an intramuscular injection of tiletamine (2 mg/kg), zolazepam (2 mg/kg), ketamine (2 mg/kg), and xylazine (0.4 mg/kg).
Check the depth of anesthesia by ensuring unconsciousness and absence of pedal reflex, corneal reflex, pupillary reflex, and palpebral reflex.
Ensure regular heart and respiration rates.
Transport the sedated animal to the operating room on a lift trolley.
Place the animal on the operating table on its left side for surgery on the right eye.
Adjust the animal's head using styrofoam pads to achieve horizontal alignment of the central retina parallel to the floor.
Insert 0.5% proparacaine hydrochloride ophthalmic solution into the conjunctival sac three times, one minute apart.
Insert a vein cannula and intubate the animal with an endotracheal tube for inhalation maintenance anesthesia (1.5% isoflurane).
Use an anesthesia machine equipped with a patient monitor to maintain anesthesia.
Administer an intramuscular injection of Eficur per 16 kg body weight and 20 mg of Depo-Medrol approximately 15 minutes before eye surgery.
Maintain physiological body temperature during surgery by covering the animal with isothermal foil.
Monitor the animal's temperature, heart rate, and blood oxygen saturation using an ear clip and patient monitor throughout the surgery.
Ensure that the body temperature does not drop below 38 °C during the procedures.
Maintain oxygen saturation above 96% and pulse rate between 70-90 beats per minute during the entire experiment.
Turn off the flow of isoflurane and extubate the animal when the surgery is complete.
Transfer animals to their pens after spontaneous breathing and awakening from anesthesia.
Cut the 30 µm wide oval frame from a bi-axially oriented PET foil using a femtosecond laser.
Prepare poly(L-lactide-co-DL-lactide) (LLA/DLLA 90/10, MW 868, 270 g/mol) polymer solution in pyridine at a concentration of 11 wt% with the addition of 2.2 µl formic acid per 1 g of solution.
Deposit the first layer of nanofibers on a silicon substrate by electrospinning.
Place the frame on the first layer of nanofibers.
Deposit the second layer of nanofibers to complete the membrane preparation.
Deposit each layer for 7 min to reach a total membrane thickness of 3.7 µm.
Use parameters: 20 G all steel needle, voltage of 7.1 kV, gap of 10 cm, flow rate of 250 µL/min, and temperature of 25.0 °C ± 0.5 °C to obtain the membrane composition.
Remove the membrane with embedded frame from silicon substrate.
Fix the membrane to a commercial 12 well cell culture insert devoid of original membrane.
Treat nanofibrous membrane in air-plasma for 30 s at power of 70 W in plasma cleaner before seeding cells.
Isolate primary hRPE cells from human donor eyes using an enzymatic treatment of retina for 30 min.
Culture primary hRPE cells (passage 0) up to 2 weeks in DMEM/F12 supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Change the medium to 1% FBS once cell cultures reach confluency.
Culture cells for an additional 30 days in 1% FBS.
Seed primary hRPEs onto trans-well plates at a density of 2,000 cells/mm².
Seed primary hRPEs onto laminin-coated nanofibrous cell carriers at a density of 2,000 cells/mm².
Culture the seeded cells in 1% FBS for an additional 30 days.
Use the cell carriers with primary hRPEs for subretinal implantation into minipigs.
Generate hiPSC-RPE cells from MERTK associated retinitis pigmentosa patient-derived fibroblasts using CRISPR/Cas9 gene correction on two alleles (RP1-FiPS4F1-GC2).
Use control hiPSC-RPE cells derived from the fibroblasts of a healthy subject (Ctrl2-FiPS5F2).
Differentiate both hiPSC cell lines toward RPE cells.
Plate hiPSC-RPEs at 200,000 cells/cm² on laminin-coated cell culture inserts with nanofibrous membranes.
Culture the hiPSC-RPE for 8 weeks to encourage polarized growth.
Prepare a plastic capillary with a rectangular cross-section of 2.8 mm x 0.8 mm by blow molding from a plastic tube of OD 1.75 mm/ID 1.10 mm.
Cut a 4 mm x 2.2 mm loading window in the plastic capillary 6 mm from the end.
Assemble the injector using the plastic capillary, silicone handle, steel blade plunger, and piston.
Load the carrier into the injector through the loading window.
Eject the carrier into the subretinal space by pushing the plunger.
Fill a small plastic Petri dish with 2 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Place an insert with the prepared cell layer on a semi-soft polystyrene dish and center it under a light microscope.
Cut out the carrier along the oval frame using a custom-modified punch, resulting in dimensions of 2 mm x 5 mm.
Fill the injector's loading window with PBS.
Release the sample from the bottom of the dish using forceps, lift it from the liquid, and transport it to the window of the injector.
Check the side orientation marks on the frame first to detect the top side of the carrier with adherent cells.
Position the carrier in the window of the injector using a dental probe.
Push the carrier into the closed and safe upper part of the injector with the plunger.
Prepare the carrier for surgery, checking its side orientation at each step.
Unload the nanofibrous carrier from the injector by pushing the metal plunger.
Sterilize the reusable surgical instruments with a mobile autoclave steam sterilizer or similar according to a standard protocol.
Apply 1% tropicamide solution eye drops and 10% phenylephrine hydrochloride solution in the conjunctival sac 15 min before the procedure.
Shave the area around the eye using a single-use shaving razor.
Disinfect the conjunctival sac with 5% povidone-iodine solution for 5 min.
Disinfect the periorbital area with cotton swabs by scrubbing from the eyelids to the periphery.
Repeat the disinfection process three times using a 10% povidone-iodine solution and leave on for 5 min.
Cover the operating field with the eye in the middle using a standard sterile ophthalmic drape.
Move the eyelashes away from the eye globe.
Insert the lid speculum (Liberman-type or Cook eye speculum).
Optionally, fix the nictitating membrane to the skin with 8-0 polyglactin suture.
Open the conjunctiva on the nasal side 2 mm to 3 mm from the limbus using surgical forceps and Westcott conjunctival scissors.
Insert the three-valved 25 G trocars 2.5-3 mm from the limbus in the area of the pars plana at 7 o'clock, 10 o'clock, and 11 o'clock.
Use rotating movements during the insertion in a slightly oblique manner (100°-110°) toward the posterior retina.
Keep the cornea wet or coat it with methylcellulose throughout the surgery to prevent osmotic corneal edema.
Remove the middle portion of the vitreous body using the standard three-port pars plana vitrectomy approach.
Carefully remove the vitreous behind the lens in the area of the future large sclerotomy.
Inject 2-4 mg of triamcinolone acetonide (TA) intravitreally in a volume of 50-100 µL to stain the posterior vitreous.
Perform a subretinal injection of 0.05-0.1 mL BSS with a 41 G cannula more centrally, avoiding bleb formation toward the periphery.
Reduce the intraocular pressure settings to 15 mmHg during the subretinal injection to prevent transient retinal vascular occlusion.
Perform a linear large endodiathermy of the retina with a 27 G endodiathermy probe, 3 mm near the nasal bleb base.
Make a 3 mm large retinotomy with a 25 G MVR blade or vertical scissors under an intraocular pressure (IOP) setting of up to 60 mmHg for 3 min to 5 min.
Ensure no bleeding from the retinotomy before reducing IOP to 25 mmHg.
Carry out exodiathermy of episcleral vessels between two nasal trocars, 2.5-3 mm from the limbus with a 27 G endodiathermy probe by gently touching the sclera surface.
Check fluid level in the infusion bottle before enlarging the sclerotomy due to temporary high fluid consumption post-enlargement.
Make a 3.0 mm large sclerotomy, 3 mm from the limbus, using a 2.75 mm phaco knife.
Coagulate damaged vessels with a 27 G endodiathermy probe if bleeding occurs from scleral or ciliary body vessels inside the large sclerotomy.
Enlarge the sclerotomy to 3.0 mm with a satin knife to accommodate the tip of the injector (0.8 mm x 2.8 mm).
Remove the prolapsed vitreous body on the site of the large sclerotomy with a vitrector.
Maintain the infusion of BSS at the level of 25-30 mmHg with the vitrectomy system to avoid globe collapse.
Gently insert the injector with the dominant hand into the vitreous cavity through the large sclerotomy.
Enlarge the size of the sclerotomy if resistance is encountered.
Implant the cell carrier through the retinotomy into the subretinal space.
Use a bimanual technique with an additional sclerotomy and chandelier light to improve control of the implantation, if necessary.
Withdraw the injector from the eye.
Close the large sclerotomy with an 8-0 polyglactin suture to avoid complications associated with intraocular hypotony.
Perform a complete fluid-air exchange (FAX) and drainage of the subretinal fluid with a silicone-tipped cannula.
Inject silicone oil (1,000 cSt) into the vitreous cavity using the vitrectomy system and tubing system for silicone oil injection until the IOP is normal.
Perform a video recording during the entire surgery.
Document key steps of implantation using photo documentation.
Complete the fundus drawing by documenting the location of the sclerotomies, retinotomy, subretinal implant, and any complications that occurred using fundus drawing schemas.
Remove the trocars at the end of surgery.
Close three sclerotomies and conjunctiva with 8-0 polyglactin sutures.
Rinse the conjunctival sac with 5% povidone-iodine solution.
Perform a subconjunctival injection of 20 mg gentamicin, 2 mg dexamethasone, and 2% xylocaine in 0.3 mL volume.
Check the fundus and lens using microscopic view.
Remove suture(s) from nictitating membrane (optional).
Apply neomycin ointment or ofloxacin ophthalmic ointment into conjunctival sac.
Apply topical bacitracin zinc/hydrocortisone acetate/neomycin sulfate or 0.3% ofloxacin into the conjunctival sac five times per day.
Check turgor of the soft tissues of the eye using palpation postoperatively.
Inspect for inflammatory reaction on the eye surface postoperatively.
Observe squinting as a protective reaction of the eyelids using a hand-held slit lamp or indirect ophthalmoscope.
Inject intramuscularly ceftiofur hydrochloride at 3 mg/kg BW (1 mL/kg) on the second and third day of stability.
Inject tulathromycin at 1 mL/40 kg BW after 72 h post-surgery for prevention of secondary bacterial infection.
Perform an intramuscular injection of flunixin at 2 mL/45 kg live weight every 24 h for 3 days after surgery to prevent pain.
Ensure minipigs have free access to water and standard feeding twice per day.
Maintain minipigs in a specialized air-conditioned facility with a temperature range of 18-22 °C.
Keep an artificial light/dark regime of 13 h/11 h for the minipigs.
Induce sedation in the minipig by intramuscular injection of a TKX mixture.
Instill 1% tropicamide eye drops into the conjunctival sac of the minipig.
Instill 10% phenylephrine hydrochloride eye drops into the conjunctival sac of the minipig to induce mydriasis.
Use a lid speculum to maintain open eyes.
Wash the cornea with saline solution (0.9% NaCl) every 30-60 seconds.
Position the minipig on the operating table with the head placed sideways and perpendicular to the scanning piece of the OCT device.
Stabilize the minipig's head using styrofoam pads under the snout to bring the eye surface into a horizontal position.
Collect color fundus images with a color non-mydriatic fundus camera.
Take a red-free image of the retina with the non-mydriatic fundus camera.
Perform optical coherence tomography imaging using the spectral-domain OCT system.
Tilt the minipig's head manually toward the OCT lenses or fundus camera lenses to optimize the view of the posterior retina and the area of implantation.
Apply the infrared reflectance light of the OCT device to focus on the implant.
Use the OCT crossline scanning mode.
Use the OCT retina map scanning mode.
Apply ofloxacin ophthalmic ointment at the end of the examination under the lid of the animal's eye.
Move the minipig to the indoor facility and observe for its general condition until the end of sedation.
Sedate the minipigs with an intramuscular injection of the TKX mixture followed by an intravenous bolus application of 1% propofol (20 mL/animal).
Exsanguinate the animals after administering propofol.
Enucleate the eyes post mortem using surgical scissors and surgical forceps.
Remove the upper and lower eye lids using forceps and scissors.
Remove the third eye lid and cut through the conjunctiva.
Cut the eye muscles and the optic nerve.
